Nicknamed "'''Iso Joe'''", he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]]. After two years with Arkansas, he declared for the [[2001 NBA draft]] where he was drafted 10th overall by the [[Boston Celtics]]. Johnson was a seven-time [[NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star]] and also played for the [[Phoenix Suns]], [[Atlanta Hawks]], [[Brooklyn Nets]], [[Miami Heat]], [[Utah Jazz]] and [[Houston Rockets]], while also representing the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]]. While playing for the Hawks, he earned the nickname "Iso Joe" for his skills on [[Glossary of basketball terms#I|isolation plays]]. He is one of 52 NBA players to score 20,000 career points.{{cite web|first=Rob|last=Mahoney|title=How 'Iso Joe' keeps reinventing himself|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2017/05/04/joe-johnson-evolution-iso-joe-utah-jazz-nba-playoffs|website=SI.com|date=May 4, 2017|access-date=May 4, 2017}} At the time of his retirement, Johnson was the last active player in the NBA to have shared the court with [[Michael Jordan]].{{cite web | title="Last active player to have shared a court with Michael Jordan": Joe Johnson on the brink of closing a chapter | date=March 24, 2022 | url=https://thesportsrush.com/last-active-player-to-have-shared-a-court-with-michael-jordan-joe-johnson-on-the-brink-of-closing-a-chapter/ }} ==Early life== Born in [[Little Rock, Arkansas]], Johnson was a member of the William E. Thrasher [[Boys & Girls Clubs of America|Boys & Girls Club]] as a child {{cite web|title=Hawks Community News – 2008–09 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/joe-johnson-1.html |work=NBA.com |access-date=April 3, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121210192543/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/joe-johnson-1.html |archive-date=December 10, 2012 }} and attended [[Little Rock Central High School]], a school that had produced other professional athletes including Baseball Hall of Famers [[Brooks Robinson]] and [[Bill Dickey]], as well as football player [[Fred Williams (defensive lineman)|Fred Williams]] and collegiate football coach [[Houston Nutt]]. In his senior year, he led the Tigers to a state title, averaging 18.5 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 5.2 assists, and was named Arkansas Mr. Basketball.{{cite web | title=Joe Marcus Johnson (1981–) | url=https://encyclopediaofarkansas.net/entries/joe-marcus-johnson-6970/ }} ==College career== In his freshman season at [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] in 1999–2000, Johnson was named to the SEC All-Freshman team and SEC All-Tournament team after averaging 16.0 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 2.0 steals per game. Johnson led Arkansas to the [[2000 SEC men's basketball tournament]] championship.{{cite web|title=Joe Johnson Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/joe-johnson-1.html |work=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=April 3, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121210192543/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/joe-johnson-1.html |archive-date=December 10, 2012 }} In his sophomore season in 2000–01, Johnson was named to the All-SEC second team and SEC All-Tournament team, while also receiving honorable mention All-American honors. In 30 games, he averaged 14.2 points, 6.4 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.4 steals per game. ==Professional career== ===Boston Celtics (2001–2002)=== Following his sophomore season at Arkansas, Johnson declared for the [[2001 NBA draft]] where he went on to be selected with the 10th overall pick by the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|title=2001 NBA DRAFT SELECTIONS|url=http://www.nba.com/draft2001/teams/overview_celtics.html?nav=ArticleList|work=NBA.com|access-date=February 26, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080113041426/http://www.nba.com/draft2001/teams/overview_celtics.html?nav=ArticleList|archive-date=January 13, 2008|url-status=dead}} Through the first half of the [[2001–02 NBA season|2001–02 season]], Johnson played 48 games for the Celtics and made 33 starts, as he averaged 6.3 points, 2.9 rebounds and 1.5 assists per game. He was later traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] on February 20, 2002, along with [[Randy Brown (basketball)|Randy Brown]], [[Milt Palacio]] and a first-round pick in exchange for [[Rodney Rogers]] and [[Tony Delk]].{{cite web|title=Suns acquire Joe Johnson; Celtics acquire Rodney Rogers and Tony Delk|url=http://nbatrades.tumblr.com/post/31141185872/suns-acquire-joe-johnson-celtics-acquire-rodney|work=NBATrades.Tumblr.com|date=February 20, 2002|access-date=April 3, 2009}} ===Phoenix Suns (2002–2005)=== Johnson became a force with Phoenix as he averaged 14.0 points per game in his three and a half seasons with the Suns, becoming a clutch [[three-point field goals|three-point shooter]] as he averaged 39.3% from the three-point arc during his tenure with the Suns. During the 2004–05 campaign, Johnson and the Suns posted a 62–20 record. Johnson's three point accuracy improved dramatically between 2004 and 2005, shooting 30.5% on threes in 2004 and 47.8% in 2005,{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Cohen|title=The NBA Star Who Fixed His Shot—and the Knicks|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/julius-randle-knicks-nba-playoffs-11620084363?mod=hp_major_pos1#cxrecs_s|newspaper=Wall Street Journal|date=May 4, 2021|access-date=May 4, 2021}} and shooting .556 in the 2005 playoffs. In the [[2005 NBA playoffs]], Johnson required surgery to repair a left [[orbital bone]] fracture sustained following a [[Slamdunk|dunk]] attempt against the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in the second round. Johnson missed the remainder of the series against the Mavericks as well as the first two games of the Western Conference Finals against the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. When he returned, Johnson wore a face mask for protection. The Suns fell to the eventual NBA champion Spurs, 4 games to 1. ===Atlanta Hawks (2005–2012)=== [[File:Joe Johnson over John Salmons.jpg|thumbnail|right|Johnson with the Hawks in February 2010, shooting over [[John Salmons]] of the Milwaukee Bucks]] In the summer of 2005, Johnson became a highly touted restricted free agent and expressed a desire to leave the Suns to assume a larger role on the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. Johnson particularly grew upset with Phoenix's initial offers to re-sign him feeling they were well below his market value. This rift eventually led to Johnson requesting the Suns not match Atlanta's $70 million offer. On August 19, 2005, a deal was finalized and Johnson was involved in a [[sign-and-trade]] deal with the Hawks for future teammate [[Boris Diaw]] and two future first-round draft picks.{{cite web|title=HAWKS OBTAIN JOE JOHNSON FROM PHOENIX SUNS|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/Hawks_Announce_Joe_Johnson_081905.html|work=NBA.com|date=August 19, 2005|access-date=April 3, 2009}} In his first season as a Hawk, Johnson led Atlanta in several categories: points (20.2 per game), assists (6.5), steals (1.26), three-point field goals made (128) and minutes (40.7). He was one of only five players in the league to average at least 20 points and six assists in the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]], along with [[Allen Iverson]], [[Dwyane Wade]], [[LeBron James]] and [[Gilbert Arenas]].{{cite web|title=2005–06 NBA Stats: Per Game|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/leagues/NBA_2006_per_game.html|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=June 19, 2013}} Johnson was also the only Hawk to play in all 82 games in 2005–06. Johnson scored a career-high 42 points on March 7, 2006, against the [[Golden State Warriors]]{{cite web|title=Johnson gets career-high 42 points, including Hawks' first 12|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=260307001|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190209124225/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=260307001|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 9, 2019|work=ESPN.com|date=March 7, 2006|access-date=March 7, 2006}} and recorded a career-high 17 assists on March 13, 2006, against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|title=Bucks blow 17-point lead before rallying for victory|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=260313015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190209180037/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=260313015|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 9, 2019|work=ESPN.com|date=March 14, 2006|access-date=March 14, 2006}} He recorded his first career [[triple-double]] on February 1, 2006, with 15 points, 10 rebounds and 11 assists against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].{{cite web|title=Bobcats' franchise-record losing skid reaches 13|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=260201030|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211019065524/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=260201030|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 19, 2021|work=ESPN.com|date=February 1, 2006|access-date=February 1, 2006}} Johnson continued his development in the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]], when he averaged 25.0 points, 4.4 assists, 4.2 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game. His scoring average ranked ninth in the league. Johnson also shot a career-best 47.1% from the field and was subsequently named to the [[2007 NBA All-Star Game|2007 Eastern Conference All-Star]] team, replacing the injured [[Jason Kidd]].{{Cite web |title=Joe Johnson Career Stats - NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/1007/joe-johnson |access-date=2024-02-20 |website=ESPN |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2007-08-10 |title=Johnson to replace Kidd in All-Star Game |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-nba-kidd-idUSL1400182320070214/ |access-date=2024-02-20 |work=Reuters}} In 2008, Johnson made the [[2008 NBA All-Star Game|2008 All-Star Game]] as a reserve. He also was named Eastern Conference Player of the Month twice during the season.{{cite web|title=ATLANTA'S JOE JOHNSON NAMED NBA EASTERN CONFERENCE PLAYER OF THE MONTH PRESENTED BY KIA|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/Joe_Johnson_Wins_March_Player_Honors_040108.html|work=NBA.com|date=April 1, 2008|access-date=April 1, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080405215337/http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/Joe_Johnson_Wins_March_Player_Honors_040108.html|archive-date=April 5, 2008|url-status=dead}} Johnson averaged 21.7 points per game on the season, leading the Hawks to their first playoff appearance in nine years. In Game 4 of the Hawks' first-round matchup against the [[Boston Celtics]], Johnson scored 35 points, including 20 in the 4th quarter, leading the Hawks to a 97–92 victory.{{cite web|title=Hawks take care of business at home, send series to Boston in deadlock|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280428001|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017011027/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280428001|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 17, 2020|work=ESPN.com|date=April 29, 2008|access-date=April 29, 2008}} [[File:Joe Johnson Mar-2012.jpg|thumbnail|right|Johnson with the Hawks in March 2012]] Despite finishing with the worst record (37–45) among the [[2008 NBA Playoffs]] contingent, the Hawks played very even with the heavily favored and eventual NBA champion [[Boston Celtics]], taking the Eastern Conference No. 1 seed all the way to Game 7. The year marked a turning of the page for the Atlanta franchise, once considered among the least successful in pro sports. The following year, Johnson registered his second career triple-double on December 23, 2008, in a Hawks win against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], with 20 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists.{{cite web|title=Johnson's triple-double carries Hawks to win|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=281223001|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407043230/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=281223001|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 7, 2023|work=ESPN.com|date=December 23, 2008|access-date=December 23, 2008}} He eclipsed the 10,000-point plateau for his career with his first basket during a 110–107 loss to the Milwaukee Bucks on January 31, 2009, a bank shot assisted by [[Marvin Williams]].{{cite web|title=Joe Johnson wasn't aware of 10,000th point|url=http://www.ajc.com/sports/content/sports/hawks/stories/2009/01/31/atlanta_hawks_notes.html|work=AJC.com|date=January 31, 2009|access-date=January 31, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090203081504/http://www.ajc.com/sports/content/sports/hawks/stories/2009/01/31/atlanta_hawks_notes.html|archive-date=February 3, 2009|url-status=dead}} On March 19, 2010, Johnson hit a game-winning buzzer beater in overtime against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].{{cite web|title=Johnson comes up clutch as Hawks down Bobcats|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20100319/CHAATL/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=March 20, 2010|access-date=March 20, 2010}} On July 8, 2010, Johnson re-signed with the Hawks to a six-year, $123.7 million contract, which, at the time, made him the NBA's highest-paid player.{{cite web|title=Johnson signs six-year, $124M deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5365184|work=ESPN.com|date=July 8, 2010|access-date=July 8, 2010}} The signing occurred during one of the most star-studded free agency summers in league history, highlighted by [[LeBron James]]’s [[The Decision (TV program)|The Decision]]. Among others who signed high-profile deals were [[Chris Bosh]], [[Dwyane Wade]], [[Amar'e Stoudemire]], [[Paul Pierce]], [[Ray Allen]] and [[Dirk Nowitzki]]. ===Brooklyn Nets (2012–2016)=== On July 11, 2012, Johnson was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for [[Jordan Farmar]], [[Anthony Morrow]], [[Jordan Williams (basketball, born 1990)|Jordan Williams]], [[Johan Petro]], [[DeShawn Stevenson]] and a 2013 first round draft pick.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Acquire All-Star Joe Johnson|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/Johnson_Trade_Release_120711.html|work=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2012|access-date=July 11, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120720015609/https://www.nba.com/nets/news/Johnson_Trade_Release_120711.html|archive-date=July 20, 2012|url-status=dead}} After a slow start to the 2012–13 season, Johnson began to pick up his play in December, with a 32-point game against the [[Golden State Warriors]] on December 7 and a game-winning buzzer beater in double overtime against the [[Detroit Pistons]] on December 14. After scoring 33 points in a road win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] on January 2, he hit another game winner in double overtime two days later to beat the [[Washington Wizards]]. In a 113–111 victory over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on February 19, Johnson made the game-tying three-pointer with just under three seconds to go in regulation and went on to hit the game-winning pull-up jump shot in overtime. With this win, the Nets snapped a thirteen-game losing streak against the Bucks.{{cite web|first=Eric|last=Freeman|title=Joe Johnson forces overtime, follows with the game-winner to beat the Bucks (VIDEO)|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/joe-johnson-forces-overtime-follows-game-winner-beat-134045626--nba.html|work=Yahoo.com|date=February 20, 2013|access-date=February 20, 2013}} The next game the Nets played, Johnson injured his left heel and was forced to miss three games. He made his return on March 1 against the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Mazzeo|title=Nets' Joe Johnson starts in return|url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nba/story/_/id/9002616/joe-johnson-brooklyn-nets-starts-vs-dallas-mavericks|work=ESPN.com|date=March 1, 2013|access-date=March 1, 2013}} On November 15, 2013, Johnson made his first game-winning basket of the season against the Phoenix Suns as he went in for a layup to give the Nets their first road win of the 2013–14 season. On December 16, 2013, Johnson recorded a career-high 10 three-pointers in a 130–94 win over the Philadelphia 76ers. In the third quarter, Johnson scored 29 points on 10-of-13 shooting from the field including 8-of-10 three-pointers.{{cite web|title=Notebook: Nets 130, Sixers 94|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131216/PHIBKN/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=December 17, 2013|access-date=December 17, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219023423/http://www.nba.com/games/20131216/PHIBKN/gameinfo.html|archive-date=December 19, 2013|url-status=dead}} On January 2, 2014, after the Nets were down by sixteen points, Johnson made his second game-winning basket of the season to lead the Nets to a 95–93 win to give [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] its second home loss of the season.{{cite web|title=Notebook: Nets 95, Thunder 93|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140102/BKNOKC/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=January 3, 2014|access-date=January 3, 2014}} Johnson later earned his seventh [[2014 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star game]] selection. [[File:Joe Johnson Brooklyn Nets.jpg|thumb|right|Johnson with the Nets in 2014]] In just the second game of the [[2014–15 Brooklyn Nets season|2014–15 season]] on November 1, Johnson scored a season-high 34 points on 14-of-23 shooting to help the Nets defeat the Detroit Pistons, 102–90.{{cite web|title=Nets earn first win, beat Pistons Interactive, Inc.|date=February 25, 2016|access-date=February 25, 2016}} ===Miami Heat (2016)=== On February 27, 2016, Johnson signed with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|title=HEAT Signs Joe Johnson|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-joe-johnson|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 27, 2016|access-date=February 27, 2016}} The next day, he made his 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160227105223/http://www.nba.com/games/20160228/MIANYK/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 27, 2016|url-status=dead}} In his second game for the Heat on March 1 against the Chicago Bulls, Johnson scored 24 points and passed [[Reggie Theus]] for 50th on the NBA's career scoring list.{{cite web|title=Heat set franchise shooting record, roll past Bulls 129–111|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160301/CHIMIA/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=March 1, 2016|access-date=March 1, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303112741/http://www.nba.com/games/20160301/CHIMIA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 3, 2016|url-status=dead}} On March 12, he scored a season-high 28 OT|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160312/MIATOR/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=March 12, 2016|access-date=March 12, second round of the playoffs, where they were defeated 4–3 by the Raptors. ===Utah Jazz (2016–2018)=== On July 8, 2016, Johnson signed a two-year, $22 million contract with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|title=Jazz Sign Free Agent Joe Johnson|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-free-agent-joe-johnson|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2016|access-date=July 8, 2016}}{{cite web|title=Reports: Joe Johnson, Utah agree on 2-year, $22 million deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/16691520/joe-johnson-utah-jazz-reach-agreement-two-year-deal-worth-22-million-according-multiple-reports|work=ESPN.com|date=July 2, 2016|access-date=November 6, 2016}} He joined the Jazz with the intention being to come off the bench behind [[Gordon Hayward]]. But with an injury to Hayward during preseason, Johnson was thrust into the starting line-up in his absence.{{cite web|first=Aaron|last=Falk|title=Utah Jazz: Joe Johnson thrust back into starting role with Gordon Hayward injured|url=http://www.sltrib.com/home/4455518-155/utah-jazz-joe-johnson-thrust-back|work=SLTrib.com|date=October 11, 2016|access-date=October 11, 2016}} He made his debut for the Jazz in their season opener on October 25, scoring a team-high 29 points in a 113–104 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|title=Lillard scores 39, Blazers run home-opening win streak to 16|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899376|work=ESPN.com|date=October 25, 2016|access-date=October 26, 2016}} With Hayward's return to line-up on November 6 to face the [[New York Knicks]], Johnson came off the bench for the first time since December 9, 2003.{{cite web|title=Hayward scores 28 in season debut, leads Jazz over Knicks|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899537|work=ESPN.com|date=November 6, 2016|access-date=November 6, 2016}} On February 8, 2017, Johnson highlighted a 27-point performance with six three-pointers on eight attempts in a 127–94 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|title=Johnson scores 27, Jazz pound Pelicans 127–94|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900194|work=ESPN.com|date=February 8, 2017|access-date=February 9, 2017}} On April 15, 2017, Johnson scored a team-high 21 points off the bench and hit a game-winning floater at the buzzer to give the Jazz a 97–95 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in Game 1 of their first-round playoff series.{{cite web|title=Jazz overcome loss of Rudy Gobert, down Clippers on buzzer-beater|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400950417|work=ESPN.com|date=April 15, 2017|access-date=April 15, 2017}} Eight days later in Game 4, Johnson again paced the Jazz with 28 points off the bench to give them a 105–98 victory and tie the series with the Clippers at 2–2.{{cite web|title=Johnson scores 28, Jazz beat Clippers 105–98 to even series|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400950421|work=ESPN.com|date=April 23, 2017|access-date=April 23, 2017}} The Jazz went on to eliminate the Clippers with a 104–91 victory in Game 7, closing out the first-round series 4–3 to earn the franchise's first postseason series victory since 2010.{{cite web|title=Jazz sink Clippers in 7 for first postseason series win since 2010|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400950426|work=ESPN.com|date=April 30, 2017|access-date=April 30, 2017}} Johnson missed 21 games early in the 2017–18 season while dealing with a right wrist injury.{{cite web|title=Gorbert, Favors hurt in Jazz's 107–95 win over Celtics|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975174|work=ESPN.com|date=December 15, 2017|access-date=December 15, 2017}} On February 8, 2018, Johnson was acquired by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in a three-team trade that involved the Jazz and the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|title=Kings Acquire Iman Shumpert, Joe Johnson, 2020 Second-Round Draft Selection, Rights to Dimitrios Agravanis and Cash Considerations in Three-Team Trade|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-iman-shumpert-joe-johnson-2020-second-round-pick|work=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2018|access-date=February 8, 2018}} Three days later, he was waived by the Kings before appearing in a game for them.{{cite web|title=Kings Waive Joe Johnson|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-waive-joe-johnson|work=NBA.com|date=February 11, 2018|access-date=February 11, 2018}} ===Houston Rockets (2018)=== On February 14, 2018, Johnson signed with the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|title=Rockets Sign Joe Johnson|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-joe-johnson|work=NBA.com|date=February 14, 2018|access-date=February 14, 2018}} He made his debut for the Rockets later that day, scoring nine points in 31 minutes off the bench in a 100–91 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|title=Kings vs. Rockets – Box Score|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400975606|work=ESPN.com|date=February 14, 2018|access-date=February 14, 2018}} ===Triplets Big3 and The Basketball Tournament (2019–2022, 2023-present)=== In March 2019, Johnson signed to play in the [[BIG3]].{{cite web |last1=Glass |first1=Connor |date=March 14, 2019 |title=Joe Johnson Joins BIG3 |url=https://big3.com/news/joe-johnson-joins-big3/ |access-date=March 14, 2019 |website=big3.com}} On August 27, 2019, Johnson was named BIG3 MVP.{{cite web |date=August 27, 2019 |title=JOE JOHNSON NAMED BIG3 MVP AND LISA LESLIE TAKES HOME COACH OF THE YEAR HONORS |url=https://big3.com/news/joe-johnson-named-big3-mvp-and-lisa-leslie-takes-home-coach-of-the-year-honors/ |access-date=August 27, 2019 |website=Big3.com}} On September 1, 2019, he won his first BIG3 championship with the [[Triplets (basketball)|Triplets]], defeating the [[Killer 3's]]. On September 19, 2019, Johnson returned to the NBA, signing with the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web |date=September 19, 2019 |title=Detroit Pistons Sign Free Agent Joe Johnson |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-free-agent-joe-johnson |access-date=September 19, 2019 |website=NBA.com}} He was later waived by the team on October 21, 2019,{{cite web |date=October 21, 2019 |title=The roster is now set for the 2019–20 season |url=https://twitter.com/DetroitPistons/status/1186398877005549572 |access-date=October 21, 2019 |website=Detroit Pistons on Twitter.com}} with final cuts looming. Johnson competed for [[Overseas Elite]] in [[The Basketball Tournament 2020]], helping them to the semifinals. He was named to the All-Tournament team.{{cite tweet |number=1283210973730484224 |user=thetournament |title=These guys were UNREAL this summer! Your #TBT2020 All-Tournament Team! |date=July 14, 2020 |accessdate=July 14, 2020}} Johnson originally retired during the 2022 BIG3 season,{{Cite web |date=2022-07-24 |title=Week 6 Saturday: Results and Recap |url=https://big3.com/news/week-6-saturday-results-and-recap/ |access-date=2023-03-01 |website=BIG3 |language=en-US}} however, he returned to BIG3 for 2023.{{Cite web |title=Joe Johnson Player Profile |url=https://big3.com/players/joe-johnson/ |access-date=2023-07-06 |website=BIG3 |language=en-US}} === Return to the Celtics (2021–2022) === On December 22, 2021, Johnson signed a 10-day contract with the [[Boston Celtics]] to return to the franchise that drafted him after the team was granted a hardship exception.{{cite web|title=Celtics Sign Joe Johnson|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-joe-johnson|website=NBA.com|date=December 22, 2021|access-date=December 22, 2021}} His appearance that same night against the [[2021–22 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]] marked a 19-year, 305-day gap between his stints with the Celtics, which is the longest gap in NBA history. He also made his lone shot in that appearance, making him the second player along with [[Dirk Nowitzki]] to score a basket with the same team at the age of 20 and at the age of 40.{{cite web|last=Chaudhary |first=Aikansh|title=Joe Johnson is the Only Active Player Who Has Played Against Michael Jordan|url=https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/joe_johnson_is_the_only_active_player_who_has_played_against_michael_jordan/s1_16751_36797219|website=yardbarker.com|date=December 22, 2021|access-date=December 23, 2021}} His sole appearance for the Celtics in 2021 would be the final appearance of his NBA career. It was his first NBA action in 1,304 days, with his last appearance before that point coming in the [[2018 NBA playoffs]] with the Rockets on May 28, 2018. With his retirement, there were officially no active players left in the NBA who had shared the court with Michael Jordan during their career. ==National team career== On March 5, 2006, Johnson was one of 23 NBA players named to the 2006–08 [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] and played for the United States national team in the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]]. He helped USA win the bronze medal by defeating [[Argentina men's national basketball team|Argentina]] in the third place game after a loss to [[Greece men's national basketball team|Greece]] in the semi-finals.{{cite news |author1=Jeff Taylor |title=Game Report, United States vs Argentina, Bronze Medal 96–81 |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/news/Game-Report-United-States-vs-Argentina-Bronze-Medal-96-81 |access-date=21 February 2021 |work=[[FIBA]] |date=2 September 2006}}{{cite news |title=Upset special: Greece stuns U.S. in FIBA semis |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/wbc2006/news/story?id=2568543 |access-date=21 February 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=1 September 2006}}{{cite web|url=http://www.landofbasketball.com/usabasketball/2006_wc_usa_roster.htm|title=USA Basketball Roster at the 2006 FIBA World Championships|work=LandOfBasketball.com|access-date=April 1, 2008}} In nine games, Johnson averaged 7.3 points.{{cite web |title=Joe Johnson's profile – 2006 FIBA World Championship |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/58457/sid/3507/tid/379/tid2//_/2006_FIBA_World_Championship/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100605084231/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/58457/sid/3507/tid/379/tid2/_/2006_FIBA_World_Championship/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 5, 2010 |access-date=21 February 2021 |work=[[FIBA]]}} In February 2021, Johnson was selected to the 14-player roster for the final round of the [[2022 FIBA AmeriCup qualification]].{{cite news |title=Isaiah Thomas, Joe Johnson headline U.S. roster for AmeriCup qualifying |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2021/02/03/isaiah-thomas-joe-johnson-headline-u-s-roster-for-americup-qualifying/ |access-date=20 February 2021 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=3 February 2021}} On February 19, he scored 11 points in a 93–77 victory over the [[Bahamas men's national basketball team|Bahamas]].{{cite news |author1=Sam Quinn |title=Isaiah Thomas, Joe Johnson combine for 30 points in Team USA victory over the Bahamas in FIBA AmeriCup |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/isaiah-thomas-joe-johnson-combine-for-30-points-in-team-usa-victory-over-the-bahamas-in-fiba-americup/ |access-date=20 February 2021 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=20 February 2021}} On February 20, he had 11 points, 9 rebounds, 7 assists and 2 blocks in a 96–75 victory against [[Mexico men's national basketball team|Mexico]].{{cite news |author1=Blake Schuster |title=Isaiah Thomas, Team USA Cruise Past Mexico in FIBA AmeriCup Qualifying |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2932742-isaiah-thomas-team-usa-cruise-past-mexico-in-fiba-americup-qualifying |access-date=21 February 2021 |work=[[Bleacher Report]] |date=21 February 2021}} career == In 2023, Johnson opened Iso Yoga, a [[hot yoga]] studio in [[Atlanta]].{{Cite web |last=Abdur-Rahman |first=Nahlah |date=2024-08-14 |title=Former NBA Star Joe Johnson Goes from Hoops To Hot providing an inclusive space for people of different ages and backgrounds. According to the studio, Johnson became interested in hot yoga after experiencing its benefits for injury prevention and recovery during his professional basketball career.{{Cite web |title=What We Do |url=https://www.isoyogastudio.com/what-we-do |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=Iso Yoga |language=en}} In 2025, Johnson joined the podcast ''[[Nightcap (podcast)|Nightcap]]'' as a co-host alongside [[Shannon Sharpe]] and [[Chad Johnson|Chad "Ochocinco" Johnson]].{{Cite web |title=Nightcap |url=https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/nightcap/id1706534198 |access-date=2026-07-05 |website=Apple Podcasts |language=en-US}} ==Personal life== Johnson's mother, Diane, was a former state psychiatric hospital nurse. She raised her only son by herself in Little Rock, benefiting from the help of a close family that included her mother and brothers.{{cite web|last=Bondy|first=Stefan|title=Diane Johnson battles rare cancer with strength and love of her son, Brooklyn Nets star Joe Johnson|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/nets/nets-star-love-strength-mom-cancer-battle-article-1.1271688|work=nydailynews.com|date=February 25, 2013|access-date=March 1, 2013}} She was diagnosed in 2008 with [[multiple myeloma]], a rare and typically incurable cancer of bone marrow plasma cells.
